g.text: 1. Self-direction — adults co-plan; ask goals first (\"what do you want from today?\")
2. Experience — build ON their years (junior midwives know labour; link, don't lecture)
3. Readiness — teach at need (cannulation the morning of cannulation lists, not last term)
4. Problem-centred — cases beat chapters (\"this breathless child — what's your ABCDE?\")
5. Internal motivation — dignity + growth + patients, not fear + marks (praise progress)
COGNITIVE
know → apply → analyse
"why this drug,
this dose?"
PSYCHOMOTOR
see → do → teach
demo → return-demo
→ supervised solo
AFFECTIVE
feel → value → live
empathy, ethics,
attitude checks
CLINICAL METHODS LADDER (low → high fidelity): bedside Q&A → demonstration
+ return-demo → case-based discussion → role-play (breaking news, de-escalation) →
simulation/scenario drills (arrest, PPH, neonatal resus) → supervised real care. Rule:
NEVER first-time-on-patient what drills can teach — manikins absorb errors, patients
mustn't. Lesson plan: objective (SMART) → prior check → teach → practise → assess →
summary + handout. Questioning: open first (\"what do you see?\"), Socratic probes,
wait 5 seconds, praise reasoning aloud — humiliation teaches hiding, not healing.
PATIENT EDUCATION (your commonest teaching): assess (literacy, language, beliefs,
barriers) → chunk (3 points max) → plain words + demo → TEACH-BACK (\"show me / tell
me how you'll…\") → leaflets/pictures → document taught + understood. Inhalers, insulin,
ORPs, wound care, TB/DOTS adherence, discharge meds — un-taught discharges rebound
as readmissions. Family included (consent), interpreters used, beliefs respected —
education imposed without listening is lecturing; with listening, it's healing.
Exam line: \"adults learn by need, experience and problems — teach the gap, not the chapter.\"
